Parent portal

The answer, without the phone call

Most calls to a school office are one of three questions: how much do I owe, was my child in school on Tuesday, and what did she get in the test. A parent can answer all three themselves, on the phone in their hand, with nothing to install.

Start 14 day free trial Open the portal
For parents

Are you a parent?

Sign in with the email address and password your child’s school gave you. You will see your own children, and nobody else’s.

Parent sign in

No account yet? Only your child’s school can create one. Contact the school office and ask them to make you a parent account: they will give you the email address and password to use. There is nothing here for you to buy and no form to fill in, and it takes the school a few seconds.

Forgotten your password? Ask the office as well. The address a school gives you does not have to be a real mailbox, so a reset email may never arrive, and the office can look your password up and read it back to you.

What a parent sees, and what they cannot

Their own children, all of them

One login for the family. A father with three children in the school sees all three, with one combined balance and the per child breakdown underneath, which is the same shape as the receipt he was handed.

Every receipt, not just the balance

The full history: what was charged, what was paid, when, and by which receipt number. A parent who thinks a payment is missing can check before they ring, and usually finds it.

Attendance day by day

Present, absent, late, half day or leave, per day. Not a percentage with no detail behind it, because a percentage is exactly what starts the argument a school wants to avoid.

Results, once you release them

Nothing appears until the school publishes it. Marks being entered and results being visible are two separate events, so a teacher can work on Tuesday and the school can announce on Friday.

A parent cannot see another family's child. Not because a menu is hidden: a parent account has no direct access to any table at all, and every read it makes goes through a function scoped to that parent's own children. A parent who tried a different address would get nothing back rather than somebody else's data.

Two things it deliberately does not do

  • Parents cannot pay through it. Cash, bank transfer and wallet payments are all recorded by the office, but there is no online payment for school fees. Saying so costs a few visitors and saves every one of them a surprise.
  • Parents cannot open their own account. The school creates the login and hands it over, which is deliberate: an open registration form on a page listing children is not something a school should have to police.
